finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches a fully attacker-controlled URL server-side with no validation. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), localhost, and other non-public hosts. Redirects are followed by default, and the first 500 characters of the response body and the status code are returned to the caller, so the SSRF is non-blind and data is exfiltrated directly.
finding.source: Flask query parameter `url` (request.args.get("url")) at app.py:15, unauthenticated

trace.note: Route /preview is registered with no authentication
target = request.args.get("url", "") reads the attacker-supplied URL
requests.get(target) is called with the unmodified string
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the attacker in the JSON response

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, host allowlist, resolved-IP check, or private-range blocklist anywhere on the path. requests follows redirects by default (allow_redirects not disabled). There is no auth decorator and no egress filtering in the code. The requests library only supports http/https, so file:// and gopher:// are not reachable, but internal HTTP and metadata endpoints are.

verdict.reason: app.py:15-17 passes the unauthenticated `url` query param straight into requests.get with no validation and returns the status and first 500 body chars; the ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner (app.py:23-25), not in /preview.
